test_data.description: Typical domestic electricity billing example with standard consumption and a normal tariff.
test_data.purpose: Verify standard bill calculation for a valid consumption case of 50 units resulting in a bill of 12.50.

test_data.description: Alternative valid billing example with higher but realistic usage and the same standard unit rate.
test_data.purpose: Confirm the system calculates a larger but valid consumption value of 145 units and bills correctly at the standard rate.

test_data.description: Boundary case where no energy was consumed during the billing period.
test_data.purpose: Verify zero consumption is accepted and results in a zero bill amount.

test_data.description: Boundary example with a zero-consumption account at a different realistic meter position and tariff.
test_data.purpose: Check the system consistently handles equal readings at a different meter value and tariff without charging usage.

test_data.description: Invalid input with negative previous meter reading while the remaining values are otherwise valid.
test_data.purpose: Verify the system rejects negative meter readings when the previous reading is below zero.

test_data.description: Invalid input using a large negative previous meter reading to confirm validation is not limited to small negative values.
test_data.purpose: Ensure the system rejects any negative previous meter reading, including larger negative values.

test_data.description: Invalid input with a negative current meter reading while the previous reading is valid.
test_data.purpose: Verify the system rejects negative current meter readings.

test_data.description: Invalid input with a negative current meter reading at a more extreme value.
test_data.purpose: Confirm the system consistently rejects negative current readings regardless of the magnitude.

test_data.description: Invalid case where the current meter reading is lower than the previous meter reading by 1 unit.
test_data.purpose: Verify the system rejects decreasing meter readings, including the smallest invalid difference.

test_data.description: Invalid case with a larger decrease between previous and current readings to confirm the same validation rule applies.
test_data.purpose: Ensure the system rejects any current reading lower than the previous reading, not just by one unit.

test_data.description: Boundary case where the current meter reading equals the previous reading at a low valid meter value.
test_data.purpose: Confirm the system accepts equal readings as valid and calculates zero consumption.

test_data.description: Boundary case with equal readings at a higher meter value and a different tariff.
test_data.purpose: Check that equality validation works consistently across different meter values and rate inputs.

test_data.description: Valid billing example using a decimal unit rate and small non-zero consumption.
test_data.purpose: Verify the system handles fractional tariffs correctly and calculates bill amount for 12 units of usage.

test_data.description: Valid billing example with decimal tariff and a realistic moderate consumption amount.
test_data.purpose: Confirm decimal rate multiplication remains accurate for a larger valid consumption of 87 units.

test_data.description: Boundary-negative case where the current reading is lower than the previous reading by exactly 1 unit.
test_data.purpose: Validate rejection at the minimum possible invalid difference.

test_data.description: Boundary-negative case where the current reading is lower than the previous reading by exactly 1 unit at a higher meter value.
test_data.purpose: Ensure the same one-unit decrease validation is applied consistently regardless of the absolute meter value.

unclear_requirements: The business rules do not specify whether meter readings must be whole numbers only or whether decimal readings are allowed.
The business rules do not specify the exact validation message text to be displayed for rejected readings.
The business rules do not specify whether the system should prevent entry of a negative unit rate or zero unit rate.
The business rules do not specify rounding rules or number of decimal places for bill amounts.
The business rules do not specify whether the system should validate missing/blank readings.
